definitions.explanation: A style of sushi in which various toppings such as raw fish, egg, and vegetables are scattered over a bed of vinegared rice in a bowl.

examples.japanese: ちらし{寿司|ずし}を{作|つく}る。
{昼|ひる}ごはんにちらし{寿司|ずし}を{食|た}べた。
ひな{祭|まつ}りには{家族|かぞく}でちらし{寿司|ずし}を{作|つく}って{食|た}べるのが{我|わ}が{家|や}の{習慣|しゅうかん}だ。
examples.english: It's our family's tradition to make and eat chirashi-zushi together on Girls' Day.

notes:
FORMS:
ちらし (scattering, from ちらす "to scatter") + {寿司|ずし}. Named for the way toppings are scattered over the rice.
Toppings and style vary by region. Edo-style (Tokyo) features raw fish sliced on top, while other regions may mix ingredients into the rice.

CULTURAL NOTE:
A popular dish for celebrations, especially ひな{祭|まつ}り (Girls' Day, March 3). Home-made versions often feature {錦糸|きんし}{卵|たまご} (thin egg strips), {海老|えび} (shrimp), and {蓮根|れんこん} (lotus root). Restaurant versions typically feature sliced raw fish.
